source.title: On the Joint Interaction of Models, Data, and Features
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Christina Baek; J. Kolter

record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-model feature alignment using PCA-projected activation correlations and clustered shared features, rather than directly applying the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study measures similarity of features across independently trained models and reports how it differs by training-set size and architecture. GDE accuracy/agreement results and feature-frequency/confidence findings are not representation-alignment results, so they are not rows here. Values visible only in plots are recorded from the authors’ textual descriptions.
record.test_reason: It measures cross-seed feature overlap in ResNet18 ensembles on CIFAR-10, using correlations between PCA-projected penultimate features (a PCA variant of Li et al.'s matching), and compares 10k- and 45k-trained collections. The paper's main aim is a feature-learning framework for GDE; the alignment results are secondary and mostly in the appendix.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the paper's central conclusion is the feature-learning framework. It explains GDE without assuming calibration and predicts when GDE breaks (class merging preserves it; blue-intensity partitions break it). The convergence-related findings are supporting observations: 45k models share more top features, and models sharing features share errors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PCA of last-layer activations, correlation-based feature clustering, and an interaction tensor; it does not reproduce either original source’s method. The comparison across 10k and 45k changes training-set size, not model parameter scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report qualitative feature-clustering results are not very sensitive to gamma_corr values 0.75, 0.80, 0.9, and 0.95. Feature alignment is described as greater for the 45k than the 10k collection.

fits_no_version.finding: Model pairs that share more PCA features have a higher lower bound on shared errors, for same-architecture (45k, 10k) and different-architecture pairs. Low feature overlap does not guarantee low shared error across architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Degree of shared representation predicts how far models' errors are correlated.

record.problems: The model-alignment findings are qualitative and figure-based, with no numerical similarity estimates or uncertainty reported for those comparisons. The size/performance comparison changes training-data quantity, not model size. The diverse-architecture result is an aggregate across model pairs, and the paper does not establish why the features align.
record.rows_left_out: Section 6, Tables 1–2, and related appendix results report accuracy, agreement, and GDE under class-merging and data-partition interventions; these do not measure representation convergence. Other feature-frequency, confidence, and nearest-neighbor findings likewise do not compare representations across models.

untested.parts: Model parameter scale; different architectures, objectives or data sources becoming more aligned with capability.
Whether individual units or bases differ. Only PCA components are compared, and the text notes the components are naturally aligned by variance ordering.
Alternative similarity measures, input distributions, out-of-distribution inputs. The threshold statement is too unspecific to judge.
Plateau with scale. The causal role of shared data is only indirectly suggested (O.3).

missing.what: Number of feature clusters versus total features. 20 models × 50 PCs = 1000 features collapse to T=680 clusters for 45k, a quantitative indicator of partial cross-seed sharing.
Number of models learning a feature correlates strongly (linear/super-linear) with how often the feature appears in data. Frequent features are shared across seeds; rare tail features are not.
Same-architecture shared errors are far above chance (>35% at 45k), and the text says the shared-feature/shared-error pattern holds for SVHN too.

record.verdict_notes: r3–r5 were relinked to none because they measure the feature–error relationship, not convergence. The V6 'challenges' label was dropped because the threshold-insensitivity statement is generic and gives no per-threshold alignment values. Figure 7 shows only a few random model pairs, and no numbers are given for cross-model similarity.

versions.untested_parts: Tests increased training-data quantity and accuracy for one architecture, not larger model parameter counts or convergence across different objectives, training data sources, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation alignment is measured.
Tests shared PCA-derived features and feature overlap across seeds, but not whether individual units or bases differ.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment method is tested.
The study defines features as principal components and clusters correlated components; it does not test recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests sensitivity to the feature-correlation clustering threshold only; does not compare other similarity measures or systematically vary the input distribution, including out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not vary shared training data or objectives to identify their causal contribution, nor test plateau or incomplete convergence as a function of model scale.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (20-model collection; pairwise representation correlations)
rows.operation_detail: Compared correlations between PCA-projected penultimate-layer features across models.

conditions.value: 20 models; correlation matrices shown for model pairs

rows.value: The correlations for 10k models show less structure than those for 45k models.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison from the text accompanying the figure; no numerical similarity value is reported.
rows.check: Serves as the low-data baseline for r2. Some cross-model structure remains, but less than at 45k (Fig. 7). Qualitative only.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, experimental setup; Appendix E.1, Figure 7 caption and accompanying discussion.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (20-model collection; pairwise representation correlations)
rows.operation_detail: Compared correlations between PCA-projected penultimate-layer features across models.

conditions.value: 20 models; correlation matrices shown for model pairs

rows.baseline: 10k models: less structure in the correlation matrices
rows.value: The 45k correlation matrices have more structure, with non-zero entries more concentrated near the diagonal; the authors say the models learned nearly the same top features.
rows.note: Qualitative figure result stated in the accompanying text. The main text reports 45k average test accuracy as 84.5%; the 10k average is 67.9%.
rows.check: V1 link is narrow. All models are ResNet18 trained on random CIFAR-10 subsets of different size, so the capability axis is training data and accuracy, not scale or architecture.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4: twenty models per collection, 67.9% and 84.5% average test accuracy; Appendix E.1, Figure 7 and accompanying discussion.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (20-model collection; pairwise comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Related the number of clustered features shared by model pairs to their shared errors.
rows.measure: Shared feature count versus shared error
rows.baseline: Chance shared error for a 10-class classification problem is discussed as much lower than the reported errors.
rows.value: The lower bound of shared error is described as almost monotonically increasing with the number of shared features; shared errors vary more when fewer features are shared.
rows.note: The plot aggregates model pairs; the authors state shared errors above 35% are far above chance for a 10-class problem.
rows.check: Measures how shared-feature count relates to shared errors, not whether models converge in representation. This is a prediction-dependence construct.

rows.subject: ResNet18 (20-model collection; pairwise comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Related the number of clustered features shared by model pairs to their shared errors.
rows.measure: Shared feature count versus shared error
rows.value: Shared errors are generally smaller and show more variance than for 45k models; the authors suggest agreement behaves more randomly when model performance is lower.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison stated in the text; numerical values are not given.
rows.check: Same shared-feature vs shared-error construct, for the 10k collection. It does not measure convergence.

rows.subject: Pairs of models with different architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Related shared PCA-derived feature counts to shared errors across pairs of differently architected models.

conditions.value: Models from the testbed created by reference [39]

rows.measure: Shared feature count versus shared error
rows.value: Shared error is almost monotonically increasing with shared feature count overall. For pairs sharing 1 to 3 features, shared errors tend to be lower; for 4 to 11 shared features, shared-error values appear more random. Low feature overlap does not guarantee low shared error.
rows.note: The result is an aggregate relationship across architecture pairs; the plotted values are not reported numerically.
rows.check: Same construct for pairs with different architectures. The text gives no summary of how many features cross-architecture pairs share, only the error relationship.

rows.subject: Feature-clustering procedure applied to the model collections
rows.operation_detail: Compared qualitative clustering results under different feature-correlation thresholds.
rows.value: The authors report that qualitative results were not very sensitive to the tested threshold values.
rows.locator: Appendix D, paragraph on clustering hyperparameters
rows.note: The study gives no separate numerical alignment values for each threshold.
rows.check: 'Qualitative results not very sensitive' to gamma_corr (0.75–0.95) refers to all observations in general. No alignment value is reported per threshold, and the other metric and input choices that V6 names are not varied.

relationships.reason: Higher-data, higher-accuracy models show more near-diagonal cross-model correlation, i.e. more similar top features (r2 vs r1). This rests only on a data/accuracy contrast within one architecture.
relationships.display_finding: Models trained on 45k examples at 84.5% accuracy shared more similar top features than those trained on 10k at 67.9%.

relation.reason: The study reports its own cross-model feature comparisons and contrasts alignment between lower-data, lower-accuracy and higher-data, higher-accuracy collections.

tranche.reason: PCA-projected feature correlations and clustering directly compare independently trained representations using an adaptation of pairwise feature matching.

source_check.notes: Figure 7 provides qualitative evidence without a numerical alignment score or uncertainty estimate; PCA variance ordering contributes to diagonal concentration. Collections differ in randomly sampled training subsets as well as initialization, so the contrast does not isolate initialization or capability causally.

statements.correction: Supplied version: arXiv v1, 7 June 2023; preprint under review. Figure 7: more structured cross-model top-PC correlations at 45k than 10k. Section 4: average accuracy 84.5% versus 67.9%. Table 2: standard deviations for accuracy/agreement intervention experiments; no uncertainty reported for Figure 7.
statements.problem: The feature comparison is accurate, but reviewed status is not established by the supplied text, which identifies itself as a preprint under review. Reported uncertainty concerns intervention experiments, not Figure 7 alignment.
